bib.title: Stateless Decision Memory for Enterprise AI Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Stateless Decision Memory for Enterprise AI Agents", Vasundra Srinivasan, arXiv:2604.20158v1, preprint (independent author, no venue), 22 Apr 2026.
COVERAGE: 50523 of 50523 chars read (all 16 pages, including tables, limits, threats, references). I did not read figure pixels, only captions in the text.

FIT WARNING: Partial fit. The paper is about trajectory memory inside a single regulated decision (82-96 events, 26-28k chars), not cross-session learning from experience or lesson distillation. It maps well onto: raw vs distilled memory (raw append-only log vs incremental summary), governance/auditability, and cost vs baseline. It says nothing about memory maintenance in the sense of pruning, forgetting or staleness. The only maintenance-adjacent content is that DPM deliberately does no consolidation, and the failure modes of consolidation (compounding loss, drift). Single author, 10 cases, one model, no peer review.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. DPM beats incremental summarization only when the memory budget binds. At the 20x compression budget it gains +0.515 FRP and +0.533 RCS.
 number: FRP +0.515 (p=0.001, h=+1.17); RCS +0.533 (p=0.003, h=+1.13)
 setup: LongHorizon-Bench, 10 cases (5 loan, 5 claim), tight budget 1,338 chars vs ~26,762-char trajectory, claude-haiku-4-5 as agent and judge, temp 0, paired permutation 10k resamples. DPM = one projection over the raw log; Summ-only = running summary updated per event.
 quote: "Tight FRP 0.907 0.392 +0.515 0.001 +1.17 / Tight RCS 0.800 0.267 +0.533 0.003 +1.13"
 where: Table 1, p.8
2. At moderate (5x) and loose (2x) budgets the two architectures are indistinguishable.
 number: moderate FRP -0.043 (p=0.255); loose FRP -0.032 (p=0.625); EDA and CRR delta 0.000 at both
 setup: as above
 quote: "Moderate FRP 0.907 0.950−0.043 0.255−0.17" and "at moderate and loose budgets the architectures are indistinguishable on the gated axes"
 where: Table 1, p.8
3. The mechanism is compounding loss: each summarization step discards anchors, and the discards accumulate across 82-96 steps. A raw log never consolidates, so it avoids this.
 number: none
 setup: authors' interpretation of Exp 1 and 3, not isolated by ablation
 quote: "At the tight budget the summarization operator must discard content every step; the discards compound across the 82–96 events of a trajectory; and at decision time the running summary has lost anchors a projection over the full log would still surface."
 where: Sec 6, p.8
4. Tight-budget EDA and CRR deltas are large but not significant.
 number: EDA +0.500 (p=0.065, h=+1.57); CRR +0.500 (p=0.066, h=+1.13)
 quote: "Tight EDA 1.000 0.500 +0.500 0.065 +1.57 / Tight CRR 0.900 0.400 +0.500 0.066 +1.13"
 where: Table 1, p.8. The abstract's "four axes" claim covers only the moderate and loose budgets.
5. Cost and latency: DPM is 7.4x faster at tight and 14.9x at moderate, and cheaper. At loose it is slower.
 number: tight $0.014 vs $0.165 per run (59.8 s vs 440.3 s); moderate $0.020 vs $0.129 (23.0 s vs 342.6 s); loose $0.022 vs $0.022 (86.6 s vs 57.4 s, 0.7x)
 setup: n=10 per cell. Summ-only cost is ESTIMATED from wall time and token budgets, because the harness did not record cost_usd. Small-case determinism runs gave $0.004 vs $0.016 per replay (4x).
 quote: "Tight 59.8$0.014 440.3$0.165 † 7.4×" and "†Summ-only cost estimated from wall time and per-call token budgets because the Stage-2 harness did not record cost usd"
 where: Table 2, p.9
6. Audit surface: Summ-only needs 83-97 LLM calls to be captured per decision, versus 2 for DPM. Summ-only's surface scales linearly with trajectory length; DPM's is constant.
 number: 83-97 vs 2
 setup: structural count from the benchmark (82-96 events)
 quote: "Summ-only 82–96 0 1 83–97" and "DPM 0 1 1 2"
 where: Table 4, p.13
7. Temperature 0 on the live API is not byte-deterministic for either architecture. Byte-exact replay needs pinned model version, pinned runtime and ideally a deterministic sampler.
 number: DPM large cases 10/10 unique hashes in 10 replays; small cases DPM 6/10 unique hashes, Summ-only 9/10 (loan) and 5/10 (claim)
 setup: 3 large cases (DPM only), 2 small cases (both), 10 replays each, SHA-256 of the full surface
 quote: "the live Anthropic API at temperature zero is not byte-deterministic under 10 replays on any of the cases we tested"
 where: Table 3, p.10
8. The replay advantage is structural, not empirical. One nondeterministic call (DPM) vs N (Summ-only). The measured drift only roughly fits the epsilon vs epsilon*n scaling, and small-case DPM edit distance (0.036-0.084) was actually higher than Summ-only's (0.000-0.013).
 number: edit distance 0.036-0.084 vs 0.000-0.013
 quote: "the small-case DPM edit distance (0.036–0.084) is not uniformly below the Summ-only edit distance (0.000–0.013) because the surfaces are short enough that a single token of drift dominates the normalized metric."
 where: Sec 7, p.10
9. Governance design: an immutable append-only event log is the single source of truth. Memory is a pure projection computed at decision time, with a per-claim event-index citation, so tenant isolation is structural (no shared store).
 number: none
 quote: "The log is immutable: once an event is written it is never edited, summarized, or overwritten." and "Memory does not exist as a distinct runtime object until π is applied."
 where: Sec 4.1, p.5
10. Retrofitting a stateful memory with isolation, logging and pinned replay is possible but costly, and the cost grows with sophistication. This is argued, not measured.
 quote: "Each retrofit is an engineering cost and a latent source of bugs, and each compounds with the architectural sophistication of the base memory system."
 where: Sec 10, p.13
11. TAMS rule: use DPM if replay, audit or isolation is required; else use DPM if the compression ratio is above about 10x; else either.
 number: ~10x threshold
 setup: a heuristic from 2 domains, 1 model family, n=10 per cell. Only ratios 2, 5 and 20 were tested, so 10x is interpolated.
 quote: "else if the compression ratio between trajectory and memory budget exceeds roughly 10×: use DPM."
 where: Sec 9, p.12

BASELINES
- Summ-only: incremental summarization after each event, within the budget (the "strongest stateful baseline"). Same model, budgets and seed as DPM.
- Retrieval and schema-anchored memory are NOT run here. They are said to be "dominated" in the companion paper [1] (arXiv:2604.XXXXX, a placeholder ID, not verifiable). MemGPT, A-Mem, H-MEM, GAM, MIRIX, TiMem, MEM1 and HyMem are discussed only qualitatively and never run.
- No full-context (whole log, no budget) baseline is reported. The paper never states how a no-memory baseline would score.

LIMITS
- Authors concede: residual API nondeterminism, so DPM is "necessary but not sufficient". Single-call context ceiling; hierarchical projection is future work and would reintroduce intermediate calls. DPM is "strictly weaker... in expressive power" and cannot support an agent editing its own memory mid-trajectory. It is not a replacement for corpus retrieval.
- Threats named: same-family judge (Haiku 4.5), with no cross-family check run for cost reasons; two domains only; one model; one trajectory scale (26-28k chars); n=10. The permutation p-value floor is about 0.002. No multiple-comparison correction. The pooled test is possibly anti-conservative across domains.
- Not shown: any maintenance, staleness, forgetting or update policy; learning across sessions; long horizons above 100k chars; adversarial or prompt-injection content; a real regulated deployment. The "enterprise runs on RAG because of statelessness" thesis is asserted, with industry blogs as the evidence (refs 16-19).
- Internal oddity: the Limitations section puts the context ceiling at "roughly one million tokens", while Sec 4.5 says tens of thousands of characters and Sec 12 says a window of 10^4 to 10^6 chars. Treat the scale claims with care.
- Dated: model is Haiku 4.5, so budget thresholds may shift with stronger models. The loose-budget Summ-only timing is flagged by the author as anomalous.

BUILDS ON: Event sourcing (Fowler 2005; Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2017). RAG (Lewis et al. 2020; REALM, Guu et al. 2020). MemGPT (Packer et al. 2023). A-Mem (Xu et al. 2025). The four-axis scoring (FRP, RCS, EDA, CRR) and LongHorizon-Bench come from the author's own companion paper [1]. Benchmarks cited: LoCoMo (Maharana 2024), LongMemEval (Wu 2024), MemoryAgentBench, AMA-Bench.

CODE: No code in the paper. Repo: https://github.com/vasundras/stateless-decision-memory-enterprise-ai-agents (not opened). Worth keeping is the projection prompt, p.6: "System. You are producing a decision-ready memory view over an event log for task T. Preserve every dollar amount, date, identifier, and policy limit verbatim. Cite the event index for each claim. Do not paraphrase numeric anchors. Output three sections in fixed order." Output sections: facts (each with a [n] citation), reasoning, compliance notes.

FIGURE candidate: Figure 4, p.11, "DPM minus Summ-only on each decision-alignment axis as a function of the compression ratio (ρ)... at ρ≈20 (tight) the DPM advantage emerges at Cohen's h>1.1 on FRP and RCS. Bars are 95% paired-bootstrap CIs." It shows in one picture that raw-vs-distilled only matters when the budget binds. Figure 1 (p.5, enterprise properties by architecture family) is the governance alternative. I did not view either figure.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The extraction is clean, with some missing spaces and a few dropped minus signs fused to numbers in Table 1. The abstract says "+0.52 / +0.53", while Table 1 gives +0.515 and +0.533 (rounding). The companion paper ID is a placeholder. Table 2's Summ-only costs are estimates. Table 1's n=10 uses pooled loan and claim cases, with no per-domain breakdown.
